plant.description: A water reservoir. Input u in [0,1] is pump duty and raises the level; the reservoir drains on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a noisy level reading.

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Gain magnitude and initial lag: first slope measurement discriminates zero-gain/dead-zone vs responsive system and is required to size any future holding input for target 0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with drain is correct, y rises from ~0.38 by ~0.1-0.2 over 8 s with measurable slope within 2-3 s, giving first rise-rate estimate; if flat, dead-zone or large lag is indicated.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Gain magnitude and hold input for 0.6: second amplitude discriminates whether E1 decay means strong drain requiring high hold input versus dead-zone/no-gain, which is required to size any controller for target 0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with drain is correct, y should rise from ~0.34 with clearly positive slope, reaching ~0.4-0.5 over 6 s, in contrast to E1 decay at u=0.5; if flat or falling, pump gain/dead-zone hypothesis must be revised.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Decay behavior at u=0 and drain time constant, which discriminates strong-drain vs weak-drain explanations of E1 fall at u=0.5 vs E2 rise at u=0.8 and is required to estimate hold input for 0.6 and controller integral action.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with drain is correct, y will fall monotonically from ~0.46 by ~0.08-0.15 over 8 s after ~1 s lag, giving direct drain rate; if flat near 0.46, drain-at-zero hypothesis must be revised.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: High-amplitude gain/linearity and max rise rate: third amplitude at u=1.0 discriminates linear vs saturating response and tests whether high hold input for 0.6 is feasible, required to size controller output for target.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with ~1-2 s lag and level-dependent drain is correct, y stays near ~0.33 for ~1 s then rises with slope ~0.02-0.03/s to ~0.43-0.48 over 5 s; if slope is much smaller, saturation/nonlinearity or larger drain at higher u is indicated.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Intermediate gain/linearity and hold input for 0.6: u=0.65 brackets E1 sink at 0.5 and E2 rise at 0.8 to discriminate linear pump vs threshold and refine feedforward needed for target.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with ~2s lag and level-dependent drain is correct, y holds near 0.40 for ~2s then rises with small positive slope ~0.008-0.015/s to ~0.44-0.47 over 6s; if flat or falling, threshold/hold estimate must be revised upward.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state hold input for 0.6: testing u=0.65 starting inside the band discriminates hold~0.65 vs hold~0.8 and is required to size feedforward/integral for the controller.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with ~2s lag and level-dependent drain is correct, y will stay near 0.56 for ~1-2s then rise slowly with slope ~0.005-0.015/s to ~0.58-0.60 over 4s; if y falls clearly, hold-input estimate must be revised upward toward 0.75-0.85.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state hold input for 0.6 and drain rate at high level: stepping down to 0.55 from inside the band discriminates hold ~0.60 vs hold ~0.65 and is required to size controller feedforward for target 0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with ~1-2s lag and level-dependent drain is correct with hold for 0.6 near 0.60, y will hold near 0.61 for ~1-2 s then fall slowly at ~0.005-0.015/s to ~0.58-0.60 over 4 s; if y rises or stays flat, hold <=0.55 and H6 must be revised downward.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Drain rate at operating level near 0.6 and true hold input for 0.6, discriminating strong-drain versus carryover explanations of E6-E7 rises.
experiments.expected_observation: If lag plus level-dependent drain is correct, y will stay near 0.64 for ~1-2 s of carryover then fall monotonically at ~0.015-0.03/s to ~0.48-0.56 over 8 s; if flat near 0.64, drain-at-zero hypothesis must be revised.

ledger.statement: Increasing pump duty u increases level y (positive steady-state gain).
Response to a step in u shows lag/carryover of ~1.5-2.5 s before full slope is seen, not an instantaneous jump.
There is a dead zone at low u (e.g., u < 0.1-0.2) where pump produces little or no rise.
At u=0 the level decays on its own due to drainage, ~0.03-0.036/s near 0.55-0.64 and slower at low level.
Steady-state gain is approximately monotonic in u but with level-dependent drain and ~2s second-order carryover, so raw average slopes are not perfectly linear across amplitudes.

Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.6 is ~0.48-0.58, most likely ~0.50-0.54, because u=0.55 still rose at 0.62-0.64 in E7 and u=0.65 rose at 0.56-0.61 in E6 while u=0 fell at ~0.035/s implying k~0.07/s per unit u.
Sensor noise is small relative to control band, e.g., std < 0.02 vs 0.10 band width.
